title: Ancient DNA unveils distinctive ancestries in the Bronze and Iron Ages of East Tianshan.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Europe PMC says not open access, no PMC identifier, no supplementary files, no text-mined accessions, no GEO/SRA/BioProject links, and a Zenodo search on the title/DOI returned only unrelated geology and taxonomy records. The stated deposit, BioProject PRJCA053262 at the China National Center for Bioinformation (CNCB-NGDC), returns 'The data you are retrieving is not released'; a GSA-Human (controlled human sequence archive) browse page likewise returns 'not released'. Both Science supplementary-material URLs returned HTTP 403. The paper is not listed in the Poseidon ancient-DNA paper directory, which is where reusable ancient genotype packages are catalogued.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Everything about the content: 135 ancient individuals, 11 archaeological sites, Bronze Age admixture between Yellow River millet-farmer-related and Chemurchek steppe-related ancestry, Iron Age heterogeneity. All from the abstract. The data-availability wording (deposited in the Genome Sequence Archive under PRJCA053262, 'following the regulations of the Human Genetic Resources Administration of China') came from a web search snippet of the paper, not from a page I could open.

a1_downloadable.note: FAIL. The only stated deposit is the China National Center for Bioinformation Genome Sequence Archive, project PRJCA053262, which currently returns 'not released'. Human sequence data there sits in GSA-Human, which requires a Data Access Committee application under China's Human Genetic Resources rules. No login-free download exists; Science supplementary files return HTTP 403 and nothing is on Zenodo, Dryad, PMC or the Poseidon archive.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Not assessed in files (stopped at A1). On the paper's description, the natural labels (archaeological culture, site, radiocarbon date, ancestry proportion) live in supplementary metadata tables I could not open, and the headline label 'ancestry proportion' is itself a model output, not a measurement.

a3_inputs_present.note: Not assessed in files. The inputs would be genome-wide genotypes held in an unreleased, controlled archive; the project also appears to hold only raw sequencing reads, which this project never downloads.

a4_units_stated.note: Not assessed in files. Nothing opened, so no units column seen.

a5_enough_rows.note: FAIL on the paper's own number. The unit of analysis is the individual: 135 newly reported ancient individuals across 11 sites. That is far below the ~400 minimum for classification, and the per-site counts would be in the single or low double digits.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Not assessed. A 1240K-style ancient genotype matrix for 135 individuals would be tiny (tens of megabytes), but raw read archives for 135 ancient libraries would be hundreds of gigabytes. Moot given A1.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Cannot check: no download, no API record, no released repository entry to compare against the paper's 135.

a8_label_provenance.note: Not assessed in files, but a visible risk: the paper's central quantities (ancestry proportions from qpAdm/ADMIXTURE-style fitting) are outputs of statistical models run on the same genotypes that would be the features. Training on them would be leakage by construction, exactly the A8 trap.

integration.partner_dataset: Allen Ancient DNA Resource (AADR), the standard curated table of ~16,000 published ancient and present-day genotypes
integration.join_key: genomic position on the 1240K capture panel plus individual identifier
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Could not be pursued: the 135 new individuals are not available in any genotype format, so there is nothing to join to AADR.

controls.positive_control: Would have been: recover the known east-west ancestry cline across Eurasia from principal components, and recover genetic sex from X/Y coverage. Not runnable without data.
controls.negative_control: Label shuffling across individuals. Not runnable without data.
controls.external_validation: AADR and the 2026 Molecular Biology and Evolution eastern Tianshan study would be candidates, but neither can validate a model that cannot be trained.

honest_claim_h3: No claim is possible: the genotypes underlying this paper are in an unreleased, application-controlled Chinese archive, and even if released there are only 135 individuals, so any model would be describing a sample too small to generalise.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use ancient genome-wide genotypes to predict an individual's archaeological culture, burial site and approximate age.
plain_idea.train_on: One row per ancient individual: their genome-wide genotype calls at a fixed set of common positions, plus skeletal and site metadata. The paper reports 135 such individuals across 11 sites; I could not open any file to confirm.
plain_idea.predict: The archaeological culture or site an individual belongs to, and their radiocarbon age. The true answers come from excavation records and accelerator mass spectrometry radiocarbon dating of the bones.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Archaeologists currently assign individuals to cultures by grave goods and burial style, which is slow and disputed; a genotype-based predictor would let them test those assignments. In practice the idea is dead here because the data is closed and n is tiny.

ml_idea: Considered and abandoned: classify archaeological culture and site, and regress radiocarbon date, from ancient genome-wide genotypes, with the Allen Ancient DNA Resource as extra training data and external validation. Dead because the paper's genotypes are not obtainable and the new sample is 135 individuals.

effort.compute_note: No estimates made: no file was ever obtained, so every number would be invented.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Open the stated deposit. BioProject PRJCA053262 at the China National Center for Bioinformation returns 'not released', which killed the project in one request.

verdict_reason: Part A1 fails outright. The only data deposit is China National Center for Bioinformation BioProject PRJCA053262, which is not yet released and, as human sequence data under China's Human Genetic Resources Administration rules, would require an access application even once it is; the Science supplementary files return HTTP 403 and nothing appears on Zenodo, Dryad, PMC or the Poseidon ancient-DNA archive. A5 fails independently: the unit of analysis is the individual and there are 135 of them across 11 sites. A8 is also at risk, because the paper's headline quantity (ancestry proportions) is itself a statistical model's output computed from the same genotypes that would be the features.
